reports.summary: The R14 usage handler now follows the requested conservative contract: request diffs remain request-only, and message_end usage is explicitly uncorrelated with unknown cause. I found one fail-open registry parsing issue and one meaningful regression-test gap. This was a static, read-only review; no tests or deployment actions were performed.

findings.title: An unterminated final registry record silently disappears from the selected plan
findings.evidence: _omp_family_plan uses `while IFS=$'\t' read -r file root_key members extra; do` without processing a nonempty record when read reaches EOF. Its only final completeness check is that PATCHES has at least one entry. The newly admitted 18.10.0 branch uses this parser and then adds capability 0017 independently. Thus the parser does not validate or append the final record if that record lacks a terminating newline.
findings.impact: [INFERENCE, not executed] A registry containing earlier valid rows and a final unterminated row is accepted as a shorter plan. That final family's patch and capability-selected gates disappear without an error; even a malformed or missing-patch final record bypasses validation. This is a concrete silent-shrink admission, not a complaint about the parent's currently in-progress artifacts.
findings.minimalFix: Process a nonempty final record after EOF through the same validation path, or explicitly reject an unterminated registry before admitting any plan. Do not silently skip it.
findings.focusedCheck: In an isolated controller/registry copy, resolve two valid rows with and without the final newline. Require identical complete output, or an explicit nonzero rejection for the unterminated form—never successful one-row output. Also make the unterminated last row reference a missing patch and require rejection. Main should run this through the existing selected-version controller coverage; not executed here.

findings.title: The same-model overlap fixture never populates the headers whose borrowing it claims to prohibit
findings.evidence: Section 3b sends main/main-rewrite/side payloads and asserts usage.headers and usage.responseHeaders are undefined, but none of those requests receives a header observation. All observeHeader calls occur later, under other session keys, with no subsequent message_end for those sessions. The latest request therefore has no headers to borrow. The fixture meaningfully distinguishes HISTORY_REWRITE from the side request's SYSTEM_DRIFT, but its two header assertions are vacuous. No request-row assertion currently checks `correlation === "request-only"` either.
findings.impact: [INFERENCE, not executed] Reintroducing `headers: st.last?.headers` and `responseHeaders: st.last?.responseHeaders` into the otherwise corrected usage row would still pass these fixtures. That leaves an explicitly named R14 regression unprotected despite an assertion claiming coverage.
findings.minimalFix: Give the main and interloping requests distinct synthetic request/response header observations using the existing observation entry point, establish that the latest request actually contains the interloper's header fingerprints, and then require the completion row to contain neither. Retain the existing drift assertions and explicitly assert request-only correlation on the request rows. Exclude HEADER_DRIFT rows when selecting request-diff rows.
findings.focusedCheck: Main should run `bun patches/verify-cache-prefix-audit.ts` in the isolated verification environment after strengthening this fixture. A disposable negative control that restores only latest-request header borrowing must fail; the corrected handler must pass. No provider calls are needed. Not executed here.

reports.summary: The revised R14 implementation and same-model overlap fixture satisfy the requested non-causal contract. The 18.10 controller routing, unterminated-final-row handling, explicit 0017 capability, and rejection of the 0097 repository overlay are correct in the reviewed source. The current generated representation contains 23 physical families and 58 capabilities; no missing in-progress artifact is reported as a defect. Three findings remain in the representation oracle and active documentation.

findings.title: Tree equality and reverse-to-pristine silently exclude directories
findings.evidence: tree_manifest records files with modes and hashes, and symlinks with targets, but silently skips every directory. The exporter uses this same function for unowned-edit detection and candidate/pristine digests; the verifier uses it for candidate equality, read-only controller checking, reverse restoration, and second replay. The existing verifier's structural manifest at patches/verify-patch-family-rollups.sh:270-272 includes directory entries and modes, and the project contract explicitly requires file/directory/symlink-set comparison.
findings.impact: [INFERENCE] Adding or removing an empty directory, or changing an existing directory's permissions, is invisible to all these comparisons. Consequently, the recorded PASS establishes file-byte/file-mode/symlink equality, not the complete structural restoration required by the contract. This does not contradict the reported successful run; it identifies a blind spot in its oracle.
findings.minimalRecommendedFix: Include directory entries and their modes in the shared tree manifest, following the existing structural-manifest convention. Account explicitly for parent directories legitimately introduced by owned files without weakening unowned-edit detection, then regenerate the manifests and representation evidence.
findings.focusedCheck: Main should use disposable trees to show that an extra empty directory, a missing empty directory, and a changed directory mode each change the structural manifest or fail the relevant comparison, then rerun the selected 18.10 representation verifier. Not executed by this reviewer.

findings.title: Capability completeness is checked against another generated output, not the retained capability contract
findings.evidence: The verifier compares controller patch/root ordering with manifest families and compares the controller's flattened capability union with the manifest's flattened union. It never checks that union against an independent retained baseline or compares each registry row's capability ownership with its manifest family. The exporter generates both outputs from the mutable 18.7 registry. In contrast, the existing verify-family-plan.py validates approved family ownership and exact coverage against a frozen deployed baseline.
findings.impact: [INFERENCE] Removing 0088 from both the generated registry and manifest leaves patch bytes and tree digests unchanged, so this verifier can still pass with 57 capabilities while apply.sh no longer selects verify-compaction-cache-liveness.ts. A capability-owner swap between registry rows is also invisible to the flattened comparison. The current inspected artifacts do contain all 58 capabilities; the defect is admission of a silently reduced or misowned future plan.
findings.minimalRecommendedFix: Validate the target capability union and family ownership against the independently captured retained baseline/migration contract, with 0017 explicitly represented as the allowed upstream adoption and approved root promotions preserved. Also compare per-row registry capability ownership with the manifest, rather than only comparing the flattened union. Reuse the existing independent-baseline validation pattern instead of treating a second generated file as the completeness oracle.
findings.focusedCheck: Main should confirm that removing 0088 from both generated metadata files fails before replay, and that swapping capability ownership between two registry rows fails even when the global capability union and all patch bytes remain unchanged. Not executed by this reviewer.

findings.title: Active documentation still advertises the unsafe causal contract and excludes the new routing contract
findings.evidence: PATCHES.md still describes the extension as a cache-miss attribution tool and says message_end pairs usage with the request diff to emit 'MISS CAUSED BY <KIND>'. The extension contract still names lastDiffByModel and says completion headers read st.last. The rollup contract says OMP_PATCH_PLAN is supported only for 18.7.0. These statements conflict with the reviewed implementation, which deliberately emits uncorrelated usage and supports deployed-only 18.10 routing.
findings.impact: Operators and later maintainers are directed toward the exact causal inference R14 removes, and toward obsolete version-selection rules. Historical incident descriptions can remain, but they are not currently clearly superseded by the new active contract.
findings.minimalRecommendedFix: Update the active extension and routing documentation, marking historical causal behavior as superseded. Document request-only drift, completion correlation unavailable/cause unknown, observedSessionId as context rather than request correlation, per-version registries, 18.10 deployed-only selection, rejection of 0097, and the distinction between declarative 0017 adoption and still-required native-consumer proof. Do not claim deployment or full request correlation.
findings.focusedCheck: Main should inspect the active documentation for remaining current-tense claims of diff/header attribution, per-model completion slots, or 18.7-only plan support. Historical examples should be explicitly labeled as historical rather than used as the current contract.
